harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Deployed GNU inetd 2.6 on node1 for TCP/9097. Each connection receives a dedicated handler process; PING returns PONG and other lines return ERROR. Sequential and concurrent tests pass, no handlers remain afterward, access is restricted to node2, protocol notes are unchanged, and both nodes passed serial reboot-persistence verification.
actions_performed: Built signature-verified GNU inetd 2.6 against native RHEL 10 libraries because configured repositories provided no inetd/xinetd package.
Configured inetd with tcp4, nowait.64, a dedicated non-login legacy9097 account, and the supplied handler.
Enabled a hardened systemd-managed inetd service bound only to node1's managed address.
Added a persistent firewalld rule permitting TCP/9097 only from node2.
Removed compiler packages, source trees, logs, and test artifacts after installation.
Restarted node1 and node2 individually and verified changed boot identities and full recovery.

evidence.requirement: Persistent inetd request activation on node1:9097
evidence.summary: Inetd is enabled and active, listening on 10.100.115.10:9097 with tcp4/nowait activation as the dedicated legacy9097 user.

evidence.requirement: PING returns PONG; other lines return ERROR; one request per connection
evidence.summary: Sequential tests before and after restarts returned the exact expected responses and EOF.

evidence.requirement: Concurrent clients receive separate handlers and leave no handler processes
evidence.summary: Twelve held connections produced twelve handler children parented by inetd; all returned PONG. Post-restart concurrency also passed, and final handler count was zero.
handler.py and protocol.txt retained their original checksums and metadata on both nodes.

evidence.requirement: Secure access and clean final state
evidence.summary: Firewall access is restricted to node2; no SELinux denials or service warnings were observed; build dependencies and temporary artifacts were removed.

evidence.requirement: Installed OS release and kernel preserved
evidence.summary: Both nodes remain on RHEL 10.0 with kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64.
Healthy baseline boot ID 739c9792… was captured, native reboot acknowledged, new boot ID 6223e79c… observed, and listener, firewall, files, service, and remote protocol recovered.
Healthy baseline boot ID 409baccc… was captured, native reboot acknowledged, new boot ID bf3c2d68… observed, and networking, files, kernel, and remote client behavior recovered.
